source.title: Predicting Neural Network Accuracy from Weights
source.authors: T. Unterthiner; Daniel Keysers; S. Gelly; O. Bousquet; I. Tolstikhin

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a different measurement related to model size and overfitting: rank correlations between train and test accuracy for ResNets of different widths. It does not test the listed version-specific interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper's main results predict accuracy from weights. Those predictor scores and input-perturbation results do not measure the claim versions. The ResNet train-versus-test rank correlations and the authors' interpretation of their decline with network size bear on the broader claim about model size and overfitting; cited results from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: Section 4.5 and Figure 3 report an optimizer-specific held-out performance comparison: small CIFAR10-GS CNNs trained with SGD perform significantly worse than those trained with Adam/RMSProp. This bears on V4 in a new setting. The extracted width-specific rank correlations do not test V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate: weight-based estimators predict accuracy and transfer rankings across datasets and architectures. The authors suggest a training-accuracy shortcut and interpret declining train/test rank correlations with width as increasing overfitting. That interpretation is not a direct measurement of a widening-induced test-error increase.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures rank correlations in an existing ResNet collection; it does not reproduce the listed claim-version recipes or interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: ResNet width: train/test accuracy rank correlation decreases from ×1 to ×4.

fits_no_version.finding: Train/test accuracy Kendall correlations decline from 0.83 to 0.77 to 0.64 across ResNet32 widths ×1, ×2, and ×4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across the DEMOGEN width groups, training accuracy becomes a weaker ranking proxy for test accuracy.

record.problems: The size-related result is a rank correlation between training and test accuracies, not a direct comparison of test error across widths or a measurement of the generalization gap. Uncertainty for Table 4 is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were extracted: the paper's main accuracy-prediction scores measure the predictor, not a claim-version outcome; cited studies' results are not this paper's own results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architectures and recipes.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifier performance and the contribution of local connectivity.

Controlled learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning; best achievable performance after broader tuning; matched training performance; momentum SGD, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and language benchmarks.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout versus no-dropout held-out performance comparisons. Sampling dropout rates alone does not establish its effect.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: The authors' qualitative optimizer comparison: CIFAR10-GS CNNs trained with SGD perform significantly worse than those trained with Adam/RMSProp. Add a held-out-performance comparison row, recording that no aggregate accuracy difference or uncertainty is supplied. Other hyperparameters were randomly sampled, including regularization, dropout, initialization, activation, and training-set fraction.
missing.locator: Section 4.5, Figure 3; training protocol in Section 4.1 and Appendix A.2.

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks the study's own optimizer comparison when declaring every version untested. Predictor performance, predictor sensitivity to weight transformations, and MLP transfer scores do not themselves test the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels under the same recipes.
Test-error trend when widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond the zero-training-error threshold; the paper reports ResNet train/test rank correlations by width, not that test-error trend.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparisons and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons under the specified tuning regimes.
Large- versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and with or without augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its comparison with other measures as predictors of the generalization gap.
Effect on test accuracy of removing and retraining on memorized examples.

relationships.condition: Small CNNs on CIFAR10-GS, trained for 86 epochs across randomly sampled hyperparameters without augmentation or batch normalization.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 4.5/Figure 3, missing from the rows: SGD networks perform significantly worse than Adam/RMSProp networks. This qualifies the adaptive-worse direction in this setting, although the comparison does not isolate optimizer effects or compare optimally tuned recipes.
relationships.display_finding: Reported poorer SGD performance remains unverified and does not isolate optimizer effects or compare optimally tuned recipes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
